controls.title: Use of individual external auditors and technical experts
controls.requirement: External auditors/experts operate under the CB's contract, impartiality and confidentiality requirements.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Confirm external technical experts are bound by confidentiality and conflict-of-interest rules.

controls.title: Personnel records
controls.requirement: The CB maintains up-to-date records of qualifications, training, experience and performance of personnel.
controls.security_note: CB personnel records contain personal data needing confidentiality and integrity.

extras.audit_alignment: Not a client obligation; you may request evidence of auditor qualifications.

controls.title: Outsourcing
controls.requirement: The CB retains responsibility when outsourcing audit activities and has a legally binding agreement covering confidentiality and impartiality.
controls.security_note: Outsourced audit parties gain access to client information; agreements must protect confidentiality.

extras.audit_alignment: Confirm whether any audit activity is outsourced and that outsourcing agreements protect your information.

controls.title: Public information
controls.requirement: The CB publicly provides information on its audit processes, certification process, and granting/suspending/withdrawing certification.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Read the CB's published process so audit steps and timelines are expected.

controls.title: Certification documents
controls.requirement: The CB gives certification documents identifying the client, standard, scope, and validity.
controls.security_note: Certificates are trust artefacts; accuracy and protection from tampering/forgery preserve their integrity.
controls.evidence: Issued certificate verified against scope and SoA

extras.audit_alignment: Verify certificate scope, standard version and validity dates are accurate; report inaccuracies promptly.

controls.title: Reference to certification and use of marks
controls.requirement: The CB controls use of certification marks; clients must not misuse certification or mislead about scope.
controls.security_note: Misrepresentation of certification undermines the integrity of the certification claim.

extras.audit_alignment: Use marks and certification claims only within the certified scope and per CB rules.

controls.title: Confidentiality
controls.requirement: The CB keeps information about clients confidential, has a legally enforceable commitment, and informs the client before disclosing to third parties unless required by law.
controls.security_note: Direct confidentiality obligation over client security and AI system information.

extras.audit_alignment: Agree what information can be disclosed to regulators/accreditation bodies; require notification of any legally required disclosure.

controls.title: Information exchange between a CB and its clients
controls.requirement: The CB informs clients of certification requirements, changes and audit findings; clients inform the CB of significant changes (scope, ownership, incidents, legal proceedings).
controls.security_note: Exchanged findings, incident and scope information is sensitive and must remain accurate and confidential.

extras.audit_alignment: Establish a channel to notify the CB of significant changes (e.g. major security incidents, scope/organizational changes, new AI systems) and receive CB updates.

controls.title: Pre-certification activities
controls.requirement: Application review, audit programme, audit time determination, multi-site sampling, and combined audits are defined before certification.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Provide accurate scope, sites, headcount, systems and (for AI) AI systems in scope; agree audit programme and time.

controls.title: Planning audits
controls.requirement: The CB determines audit objectives, scope and criteria, selects the audit team, and prepares an audit plan; plan is communicated to the client.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Review the audit plan; ensure interviewees, evidence and system access are arranged.

controls.title: Initial certification audit (Stage 1 and Stage 2)
controls.requirement: Stage 1 reviews documented information and readiness; Stage 2 assesses implementation and effectiveness of the management system.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
controls.evidence: Stage 1 documentation pack, Stage 2 operating evidence

extras.audit_alignment: Have documented information, risk assessment, SoA, internal audit and management review completed before Stage 1; controls operating with evidence before Stage 2.

controls.title: Conducting audits
controls.requirement: Opening/closing meetings, evidence gathering and verification, recording findings (nonconformities and opportunities for improvement), audit report, cause analysis of nonconformities and verification of corrections/corrective actions.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
controls.evidence: Audit evidence, corrective action plans, root-cause analyses

extras.audit_alignment: Provide access and evidence; agree findings; submit cause analysis and corrective action plans within CB timelines.

controls.title: Certification decision
controls.requirement: Decision is made by persons not involved in the audit, based on audit report and other information; certification granted, refused or deferred.
controls.security_note: The decision must rest on accurate, untampered audit information and impartial review.

extras.audit_alignment: Do not expect a decision at the closing meeting; ensure all major nonconformities are closed within required time.

controls.title: Maintaining certification
controls.requirement: Surveillance audits, recertification audits, special audits and suspension/withdrawal processes maintain certification over the cycle.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
controls.evidence: Surveillance-cycle plan, internal audit and management review records

extras.audit_alignment: Keep the ISMS/AIMS operating between audits: internal audits, management reviews, incident handling and change control must continue; prepare for surveillance.

controls.title: Appeals
controls.requirement: The CB has a documented process to receive, evaluate and decide appeals; appeal decisions do not lead to discrimination.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Know the appeals process if you disagree with a certification decision.

controls.title: Complaints
controls.requirement: The CB handles complaints about its own activities and about certified clients, with confidentiality.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Be prepared to respond if a complaint concerns your certified system; maintain your own complaints/incident handling.

controls.title: Client records
controls.requirement: The CB maintains records of audit and certification for all clients, kept confidential and retained per policy.
controls.security_note: Audit and certification records hold sensitive findings; they must be protected (C), accurate (I) and available for the certification cycle (A).
controls.evidence: Records retention and access-control rules for audit records

extras.audit_alignment: Retain your own copies of audit reports, findings and closure evidence; treat them as confidential.

controls.title: Options
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: The CB implements a management system per Option A (own requirements) or Option B (ISO 9001).
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Informational: the CB's own management system is audited by its accreditation body.

controls.title: Option A - General
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: The CB establishes, documents, implements and maintains a management system capable of consistent achievement of its requirements.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Informational for clients.

controls.title: Option A - Management system manual
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: Documents the management system policies and procedures.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Informational for clients.

controls.title: Option A - Control of documents
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: Controls documents so current versions are available and obsolete ones are prevented from use.
controls.security_note: Document control preserves integrity of policies and procedures.

extras.audit_alignment: Mirrors your own documented-information control; apply the same discipline to your ISMS/AIMS documents.

controls.title: Option A - Control of records
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: Maintains records demonstrating conformity, protected, retrievable and retained.
controls.security_note: Records must stay unaltered (I) and retrievable for audit (A).
controls.evidence: Records retention schedule, backups of evidence

extras.audit_alignment: Mirrors your own records control; audit evidence must be retrievable and reliable.

controls.title: Option A - Management review
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: Top management reviews the CB's management system at planned intervals.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Mirrors your own management review requirement.

controls.title: Option A - Internal audits
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: The CB conducts internal audits at planned intervals.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Mirrors your own internal audit requirement; CBs expect one completed before the initial audit.

controls.title: Option A - Corrective actions
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: The CB identifies and manages nonconformities and takes corrective action.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Mirrors your nonconformity/corrective action process.

controls.title: Option A - Preventive actions
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: The CB takes actions to eliminate causes of potential nonconformities (risk-based).
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Mirrors risk-based preventive thinking in your risk treatment.

controls.title: Option B - Management system per ISO 9001
controls.section: Clause 10 - Management system requirements for certification bodies
controls.requirement: The CB may instead implement a quality management system per ISO 9001.
controls.security_note: None - process/governance requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.audit_alignment: Informational for clients.

controls.title: Scope
controls.requirement: Determine applicability: providers, deployers, importers, distributors and product manufacturers placing AI systems/GPAI models on the EU market or whose output is used in the EU.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Operator (umbrella term covering Provider, Deployer, Importer, Distributor, Authorised Representative, Product Manufacturer) - this article determines which role(s) an organization holds and therefore which obligations apply.

controls.title: Definitions
controls.requirement: Apply the Act's definitions (AI system, provider, deployer, high-risk, GPAI model, serious incident, etc.) consistently across governance documents.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: All roles - this article is the source of the role definitions themselves (see the Role Legend above).

controls.title: AI literacy
controls.requirement: Take measures to ensure sufficient AI literacy of staff and others dealing with AI systems on the organization's behalf, considering their technical knowledge, experience and context of use.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider and Deployer - both must ensure their own staff (and others acting on their behalf) have sufficient AI literacy.

controls.title: Prohibited AI practices
controls.requirement: Do not place on the market, put into service or use AI systems for prohibited practices: subliminal/manipulative techniques causing harm, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, real-time remote biometric ID in public for law en...
controls.security_note: Emotion recognition, biometric categorisation and scraping controls overlap with data confidentiality and consent safeguards.

extras.roles: Provider (must not place on market/put into service) and Deployer (must not use) - the prohibition binds both roles independently.

controls.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Determine whether an AI system is high-risk: safety component of a regulated product (Annex I) or use case listed in Annex III, with a narrow self-assessment exemption where risk is not significant.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - responsible for classifying their own AI system before placing it on the market or putting it into service.

controls.title: Amendments to Annex III
controls.requirement: Monitor Commission updates to the high-risk use-case list (Annex III) and re-assess systems accordingly.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - must monitor for classification-list changes affecting systems it has already placed on the market.

controls.title: Compliance with the requirements
controls.section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Ensure high-risk AI systems comply with Articles 9-15 throughout their lifecycle, considering intended purpose and generally acknowledged state of the art.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - primary and direct responsibility for meeting Articles 9-15 across the system's lifecycle.

controls.title: Risk management system
controls.section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Establish, implement, document and maintain a continuous risk management process across the lifecycle: identify, analyse, estimate and evaluate known/foreseeable risks, adopt mitigation measures, and test.
controls.security_note: Risk management must cover security/adversarial risks alongside safety and fundamental-rights risks.
controls.evidence: AI risk management file, test reports

extras.roles: Provider - must establish and maintain the risk management system for the high-risk AI system.

controls.title: Data and data governance
controls.section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Apply data governance practices to training/validation/testing data: relevant design choices, provenance, collection, bias examination, gaps identification, and appropriate quality/representativeness; protect data appropriately.
controls.security_note: Poor data governance is a direct integrity risk (poisoning, bias) and can expose confidential data if provenance/access is not controlled.

extras.roles: Provider - responsible for the data governance practices applied during development of the high-risk AI system.

controls.title: Technical documentation
controls.section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Draw up technical documentation before placing on the market/putting into service and keep it up to date, per Annex IV (system description, design, development, risk management, performance, changes).
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - must draw up and maintain the technical documentation per Annex IV.

controls.title: Record-keeping (logging)
controls.section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Design high-risk AI systems with capability for automatic logging of events over the system's lifetime to ensure traceability appropriate to intended purpose.
controls.security_note: Tamper-evident, available logs are needed for traceability and incident investigation.
controls.evidence: Logging design spec, log retention records

extras.roles: Provider - must design the logging capability into the system; Deployer - relies on and operates these logs during use (see Art.26).

controls.title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
controls.section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Design systems to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret output and use appropriately; provide instructions for use with required content (identity, characteristics, performance, known limitations, human oversight measure...
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - must design for transparency and supply instructions for use; Deployer - is the recipient of this information and relies on it for compliant use.

controls.title: Human oversight
controls.section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Design high-risk AI systems, including appropriate human-machine interface tools, to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use, able to understand, monitor and intervene (incl. stop/override).
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - must design the human-oversight interface/tools into the system; Deployer - must actually assign competent human oversight during use (see Art.26).

controls.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
controls.section: Chapter III S2 - Requirements for high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Design and develop high-risk AI systems to achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, perform consistently, and be resilient to errors, faults, inconsistencies, and attempts by unauthorised third parties to exp...
controls.security_note: Direct cybersecurity obligation: protect against attacks on confidentiality (model/data extraction), integrity (poisoning, adversarial manipulation) and availability (denial of service, faults).
controls.evidence: Robustness/security test reports, resilience measures, cybersecurity controls

extras.roles: Provider - sole responsibility for designing and testing accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity into the system.

controls.title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Ensure conformity, have quality management system, keep documentation/logs, undergo conformity assessment, draw up EU declaration of conformity, affix CE marking, register system, take corrective action, cooperate with authorities.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - this article consolidates the full set of provider-specific obligations.

controls.title: Quality management system
controls.requirement: Put in place a quality management system documenting strategy for compliance, design control, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring, incident reporting, resource management, and an accountability framework.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - must establish and maintain the QMS.

controls.title: Documentation keeping
controls.requirement: Keep technical documentation, QMS documentation, conformity assessment and EU declaration of conformity documentation for 10 years after placing on the market.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - the 10-year document retention duty rests with the provider.

controls.title: Automatically generated logs
controls.requirement: Keep the logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system, to the extent they are under the provider's control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose (at least 6 months unless otherwise provided).
controls.security_note: Preserving log integrity and availability for the retention period.

extras.roles: Provider - retains logs that are under its control (contrast with Art.26, where the Deployer retains logs under its own control).

controls.title: Corrective actions and duty of information
controls.requirement: Take corrective actions or withdraw/recall a non-conforming system; inform distributors, deployers, authorised representative and, where relevant, authorities of the non-conformity and actions taken.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - must act and must notify Distributors, Deployers, the Authorised Representative and authorities as relevant.

controls.title: Cooperation with competent authorities
controls.requirement: Provide competent authorities, on reasoned request, with information/documentation to demonstrate conformity, including access to automatically generated logs where relevant.
controls.security_note: Ensure controlled, confidential handling of information shared with authorities.

extras.roles: Provider - primary duty to cooperate; an Authorised Representative may also be approached where the provider is outside the EU.

controls.title: Authorised representatives
controls.requirement: Non-EU providers appoint an EU authorised representative with a mandate covering conformity documentation, cooperation with authorities and registration duties.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Authorised Representative - this article defines its role and mandated duties, appointed by a non-EU Provider.

controls.title: Obligations of importers
controls.requirement: Verify conformity assessment, documentation and CE marking before placing a system on the market; ensure storage/transport conditions do not jeopardise compliance; cooperate with authorities.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Importer - this article sets out the Importer's specific verification and cooperation duties.

controls.title: Obligations of distributors
controls.requirement: Verify CE marking, documentation and conformity before making a system available; not make available if non-conforming; take corrective action if aware of non-conformity.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Distributor - this article sets out the Distributor's specific verification duties.

controls.title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
controls.requirement: Determine when a distributor, importer, deployer or third party is considered a provider (e.g. substantial modification, own branding) and assumes provider obligations; third-party suppliers provide necessary information/access via writt...
controls.security_note: Agreements should protect confidentiality of shared IP/technical information.

extras.roles: Distributor, Importer, Deployer or third-party supplier - any of these can be re-classified as a Provider under the stated conditions and then assumes full Provider obligations.

controls.title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
controls.requirement: Use systems per instructions, assign competent human oversight, ensure input data relevance, monitor operation, keep automatically generated logs (min. 6 months), inform provider/authorities of risks or serious incidents, cooperate with ...
controls.security_note: Deployer must protect and retain logs and monitor for security-relevant anomalies.
controls.evidence: Deployer operating procedures, log retention, DPIA

extras.roles: Deployer - this article consolidates the full set of deployer-specific obligations, the mirror of Art.16 for providers.

controls.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment
controls.requirement: Certain deployers (public bodies, banking/insurance, etc.) perform a fundamental rights impact assessment before deployment: process description, period/frequency of use, affected persons, specific risks, human oversight measures, and mi...
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Deployer - specifically deployers that are public bodies or private entities providing public services, or operating in banking/insurance, per the article's scope.

controls.title: Obligations for providers of GPAI models
controls.requirement: Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, provide information/documentation to downstream providers, establish a copyright policy, publish a sufficiently detailed training-content summary.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
controls.evidence: GPAI technical documentation, training data summary

extras.roles: GPAI Model Provider - a provider specifically of a general-purpose AI model (distinct from, but can overlap with, a high-risk AI system Provider).

controls.title: Obligations for providers of GPAI models with systemic risk
controls.requirement: Perform model evaluation incl. adversarial testing, assess and mitigate systemic risks, track/document/report serious incidents, ensure adequate cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure.
controls.security_note: Explicit cybersecurity protection obligation for the model and infrastructure against theft, unauthorized access and attacks.
controls.evidence: Systemic risk assessment, adversarial test reports, incident log, cybersecurity measures

extras.roles: GPAI Model Provider meeting the systemic-risk threshold (based on compute/capability criteria) - an elevated obligation tier on top of Art.53.

controls.title: Transparency obligations for certain AI systems
controls.requirement: Inform natural persons they are interacting with an AI system (unless obvious); mark synthetic audio/image/video/text (deepfakes) as AI-generated/manipulated; disclose AI-generated text on matters of public interest; disclose emotion-rec...
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider (must design the disclosure/labelling capability into the system) and Deployer (must make the actual disclosure to natural persons at the point of interaction/use).

controls.title: Post-market monitoring by providers
controls.section: Chapter IX - Post-market monitoring and incident reporting
controls.requirement: Establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the AI technology and risks, actively/systematically collecting and analysing performance data throughout the system's lifetime.
controls.security_note: Monitoring must detect performance degradation and security-relevant anomalies over time.

extras.roles: Provider - must establish and operate the post-market monitoring system.

controls.title: Reporting of serious incidents
controls.section: Chapter IX - Post-market monitoring and incident reporting
controls.requirement: Report serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems to market surveillance authorities without undue delay (specified timelines, incl. immediate for widespread infringement/critical infrastructure), investigate and take corrective ac...
controls.security_note: Security incidents affecting the AI system fall within serious-incident reporting duties.

extras.roles: Provider - primary reporting duty; Deployer - must also inform the Provider (or importer/distributor) and relevant authorities of any serious incident it identifies (per Art.26).

controls.title: Penalties
controls.requirement: Ensure compliance to avoid administrative fines (tiered by severity, up to the higher of EUR 35m or 7% of global turnover for prohibited-practice breaches).
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: All roles (Provider, Deployer, Importer, Distributor, Authorised Representative, GPAI Provider) - penalties apply to whichever role is found non-compliant with its specific obligations.

controls.title: High-risk AI system use cases
controls.requirement: Check whether the AI system falls under a listed high-risk use case (biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services incl. access to insurance/credit, law enforcement, migration/asylum/border, justice/democ...
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - uses this annex to classify its system (Art.6); Deployer - should also be aware of it, particularly public-sector and essential-services deployers subject to Art.27 FRIA.

controls.title: Technical documentation content
controls.requirement: Ensure technical documentation covers general description, design/development process and choices, monitoring/functioning/control, risk management measures, lifecycle changes, standards applied, and EU declaration of conformity.
controls.security_note: None - governance/process requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

extras.roles: Provider - sole responsibility for producing technical documentation to this content standard (Art.11).

controls.title: Material and territorial scope
controls.requirement: Determine applicability: processing of personal data wholly/partly by automated means, and territorial scope incl. non-EU controllers/processors offering goods/services to or monitoring EU data subjects.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Definitions
controls.requirement: Apply GDPR definitions consistently (personal data, processing, controller, processor, consent, special categories, pseudonymisation, etc.).
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Principles relating to processing
controls.requirement: Process personal data lawfully, fairly, transparently; for specified/legitimate purposes; data minimisation; accuracy; storage limitation; integrity and confidentiality; and demonstrate compliance (accountability).
controls.security_note: 'Integrity and confidentiality' is an explicit principle: personal data must be processed with appropriate security against unauthorised/unlawful processing, accidental loss, destruction or damage.
controls.evidence: Data protection policy covering all principles

controls.title: Accountability
controls.requirement: The controller is responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate, compliance with the principles.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
controls.evidence: Records of processing, policies, evidence of compliance mechanisms

controls.title: Lawfulness of processing
controls.requirement: Identify and document a valid legal basis for each processing activity (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, legitimate interests).
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Conditions for consent
controls.requirement: Where relying on consent, ensure it is freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, demonstrable, and as easy to withdraw as to give.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Conditions for children's consent
controls.requirement: Apply age-of-consent rules for information society services offered directly to children, incl. parental consent verification where required.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Special categories of personal data
controls.requirement: Do not process special-category data (health, biometric, genetic, racial/ethnic origin, etc.) unless an Article 9(2) condition applies; apply enhanced safeguards.
controls.security_note: Special-category data needs enhanced confidentiality safeguards given the higher sensitivity/harm from disclosure.
controls.evidence: Special-category processing register and conditions relied on

controls.title: Processing of criminal conviction/offence data
controls.requirement: Only process such data under official authority or with appropriate safeguards.
controls.security_note: Sensitive data requiring confidentiality safeguards.
controls.evidence: Legal basis and safeguards for criminal-data processing

controls.title: Transparency and information to data subjects
controls.section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject
controls.requirement: Provide concise, transparent, intelligible information about processing (privacy notices) at the point of collection or within required timeframes.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Right of access
controls.section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject
controls.requirement: Provide data subjects, on request, confirmation of processing and a copy of their personal data plus specified information, within one month.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.
controls.evidence: Subject access request (SAR) procedure and log

controls.title: Right to rectification
controls.section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject
controls.requirement: Allow data subjects to have inaccurate personal data corrected without undue delay.
controls.security_note: Correcting inaccurate data restores the integrity of the personal data held.

controls.title: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
controls.section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject
controls.requirement: Erase personal data without undue delay where a listed ground applies (no longer necessary, consent withdrawn, unlawful processing, etc.), subject to exemptions.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Right to restriction of processing
controls.section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject
controls.requirement: Restrict processing in specified circumstances (e.g. accuracy contested, processing unlawful) while a matter is resolved.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Notification obligation re rectification/erasure/restriction
controls.section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject
controls.requirement: Notify each recipient to whom data was disclosed of rectification/erasure/restriction, unless impossible or disproportionate.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Right to data portability
controls.section: Chapter III - Rights of the data subject
controls.requirement: Provide personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and enable transmission to another controller where technically feasible.
controls.security_note: None - rights-based, procedural or governance obligation without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Right to object

controls.title: Impact

controls.title: Prompt Injection

controls.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure

controls.evidence: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

controls.title: Supply Chain

controls.security_note: A compromised supply-chain component can leak data (C), alter model behaviour (I) or disable the service (A).
controls.evidence: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

extras.mitigations: Vet data/model sources and suppliers; vulnerability scanning of models/dependencies; maintain an AI/ML Bill of Materials (SBOM/MLBOM); use verifiable model provenance and integrity checks; monitor collaborative development platforms.

controls.title: Data and Model Poisoning
controls.requirement: Manipulation of training, fine-tuning or embedding data introduces vulnerabilities, backdoors or biases that compromise the model's security, effectiveness or ethical behaviour.
controls.security_note: Poisoning directly corrupts the integrity of the model's learned behaviour.
controls.evidence: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

extras.mitigations: Track data lineage/provenance; vet data vendors; strict sandboxing of training pipelines; use data version control (DVC); red-team for poisoning; monitor training loss/behaviour for anomalies.

controls.title: Improper Output Handling
controls.requirement: Insufficient validation, sanitization or escaping of LLM output before it is passed to downstream systems, enabling XSS, CSRF, SSRF, privilege escalation or remote code execution.
controls.security_note: Unvalidated output can corrupt downstream systems (I) or be used to trigger disruptive actions (A) via the systems that consume it.
controls.evidence: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

extras.mitigations: Treat model output as untrusted input; apply context-aware output encoding/sanitization; validate before executing/rendering; least-privilege execution of any downstream action.

controls.title: Excessive Agency
controls.requirement: An LLM-based agent is granted excessive functionality, permissions or autonomy, allowing it to take damaging actions beyond what the task requires, especially when combined with prompt injection.
controls.security_note: An over-privileged agent can be manipulated into unauthorized disclosure (C), unintended changes (I) or destructive/disruptive actions (A).
controls.evidence: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

extras.mitigations: Apply least-privilege scoping of tools/functions/plugins; require human approval for consequential actions; limit autonomous action chains; log and monitor agent actions; use sandboxed execution environments.

controls.title: System Prompt Leakage
controls.requirement: Attackers extract the hidden system prompt, exposing internal instructions, business logic, credentials or guardrail design that can then be used to bypass safeguards.
controls.security_note: Direct confidentiality risk to the operator's internal instructions and any embedded secrets.
controls.evidence: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

extras.mitigations: Avoid placing secrets/credentials in system prompts; treat system prompts as sensitive but not as a security boundary; use out-of-band guardrails independent of the prompt; test for extraction via red-teaming.

controls.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
controls.requirement: Weaknesses in how vectors/embeddings are generated, stored, or retrieved (e.g. in RAG pipelines) allow injection of malicious content, data poisoning of the knowledge base, or unauthorized retrieval of restricted data.
controls.security_note: Retrieval-store weaknesses can expose data across access boundaries (C) or let injected content corrupt retrieved context (I).
controls.evidence: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

extras.mitigations: Apply access controls/permissions on the vector store per document sensitivity; validate/sanitize ingested content before embedding; monitor retrieval patterns; isolate multi-tenant vector stores.

controls.title: Misinformation
controls.requirement: The model produces confident but false or misleading output (hallucination), which users or downstream systems may treat as reliable, leading to harmful decisions, legal exposure or reputational damage.
controls.security_note: Misinformation is fundamentally an integrity failure - the output does not reliably reflect truth or the intended knowledge base.
controls.evidence: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

extras.mitigations: Ground outputs with retrieval/citation (RAG) and require source attribution; implement automated fact-checking/cross-verification; communicate limitations to users; human review for high-stakes outputs.

controls.title: Unbounded Consumption
controls.requirement: Uncontrolled or excessive inference requests (denial of wallet/service, resource exhaustion) degrade availability or cause uncontrolled cost, incl. via model extraction through repeated querying.
controls.security_note: Directly an availability and resource-exhaustion risk, with a confidentiality dimension when used for model extraction.
controls.evidence: Test reports / control evidence for this risk

extras.mitigations: Rate limiting and quotas per user/API key; input/output size limits; monitor for abnormal usage patterns; cost alerting and circuit breakers; watermarking/output limits to deter model extraction.

controls.title: Risk (top-level definition)
controls.section: Taxonomy - FAIR core risk taxonomy (the factors to define before analysing any scenario)
controls.requirement: Define risk as the probable frequency and probable magnitude of future loss, derived by combining Loss Event Frequency (LEF) and Probable Loss Magnitude (PLM) - not a subjective high/medium/low label.
controls.security_note: FAIR risk scenarios are ultimately about the frequency and magnitude of loss arising from confidentiality, integrity and/or availability-impacting events.
controls.evidence: Risk scenario statements expressed as LEF x PLM rather than qualitative ratings

controls.title: Loss Event Frequency (LEF)
controls.section: Taxonomy - FAIR core risk taxonomy (the factors to define before analysing any scenario)
controls.requirement: Define LEF as the probable frequency, within a given timeframe, that a threat agent will inflict harm upon an asset - derived from Threat Event Frequency and Vulnerability.
controls.security_note: LEF estimates how often a CIA-impacting loss event is expected to occur.

controls.title: Threat Event Frequency (TEF)
controls.section: Taxonomy - FAIR core risk taxonomy (the factors to define before analysing any scenario)
controls.requirement: Define TEF as the probable frequency, within a given timeframe, that a threat agent will act against an asset - derived from Contact Frequency and Probability of Action.
controls.security_note: None - methodological/organizational rigor requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.
controls.evidence: TEF estimate with contact-frequency and probability-of-action inputs documented

controls.title: Threat Capability (TCap)
controls.section: Taxonomy - FAIR core risk taxonomy (the factors to define before analysing any scenario)
controls.requirement: Define TCap as the probable level of force a threat agent is capable of applying against an asset (skill and resources).
controls.security_note: Assessing an attacker's capability to overcome controls is directly about the likelihood of a confidentiality/integrity/availability compromise.

controls.title: Resistance Strength / Control Strength (RS/CS)
controls.section: Taxonomy - FAIR core risk taxonomy (the factors to define before analysing any scenario)
controls.requirement: Define Resistance Strength as the expected effectiveness of controls, measured against a baseline level of force, in preventing a threat agent from succeeding.
controls.security_note: Control strength is literally the measure of how well existing security controls resist confidentiality/integrity/availability compromise.
controls.evidence: Control strength estimate for the controls protecting the asset in scope

controls.title: Vulnerability (Vuln)
controls.section: Taxonomy - FAIR core risk taxonomy (the factors to define before analysing any scenario)
controls.requirement: Derive Vulnerability as the probability that a threat event becomes a loss event, by comparing Threat Capability against Resistance Strength.
controls.security_note: Vulnerability is the probability that an attack actually succeeds in compromising confidentiality, integrity or availability.
controls.evidence: Vulnerability derivation combining TCap and RS/CS estimates

controls.title: Probable Loss Magnitude (PLM) and the six forms of loss
controls.section: Taxonomy - FAIR core risk taxonomy (the factors to define before analysing any scenario)
controls.requirement: Estimate PLM by combining Primary Loss (direct impact to the organization) and Secondary Loss (impact from secondary stakeholder reactions, e.g. regulators, customers), categorised across the six forms of loss: productivity, response, re...
controls.security_note: Loss magnitude is the direct business consequence of confidentiality, integrity or availability-impacting events materialising.
controls.evidence: PLM worksheet covering primary and secondary loss across all six loss forms

controls.title: Secondary Loss Event Frequency and Magnitude
controls.section: Taxonomy - FAIR core risk taxonomy (the factors to define before analysing any scenario)
controls.requirement: Where secondary stakeholders are likely to react (e.g. regulatory notification, customer churn, litigation), estimate the probability of that secondary reaction and its own magnitude separately from primary loss.
controls.security_note: Secondary loss is frequently triggered by a confidentiality breach (e.g. data exposure) prompting regulatory or customer reaction.
controls.evidence: Secondary loss estimate with reaction probability and magnitude

controls.section: Process - The four-stage, ten-step FAIR risk assessment process
controls.requirement: Clearly identify and scope the specific asset (data, system, process) that is the subject of the risk scenario, at a level of granularity that supports meaningful analysis.
controls.security_note: The asset-at-risk identification frames which confidentiality, integrity and availability properties are actually being analysed.
controls.evidence: Documented asset-at-risk definition per scenario, linked to the organization's asset inventory

controls.requirement: Identify and characterise the threat community under consideration (e.g. external cybercriminals, malicious insiders, non-malicious/human error, nation-state actors) relevant to the asset and scenario.

controls.title: Stage 2 / Step 3 - Estimate Threat Event Frequency
controls.section: Process - The four-stage, ten-step FAIR risk assessment process
controls.requirement: Estimate the probable frequency of threat-agent action against the asset, using calibrated estimation (ranges with confidence levels) rather than single-point guesses.
controls.security_note: None - methodological/organizational rigor requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.title: Stage 2 / Step 4 - Estimate Threat Capability
controls.section: Process - The four-stage, ten-step FAIR risk assessment process
controls.requirement: Estimate the probable skill and resource level of the threat community relative to a defined scale.
controls.security_note: None - methodological/organizational rigor requirement without a direct CIA-protection function.

controls.section: Process - The four-stage, ten-step FAIR risk assessment process
controls.requirement: Estimate the strength of controls protecting the asset against the threat community in scope, calibrated against the same scale used for Threat Capability.

controls.title: Anticipate and prevent privacy-invasive events before they happen

controls.title: Make privacy a stated organizational commitment

controls.security_note: Feeding incident lessons back into design standards preserves the integrity of the privacy-engineering process over time.

controls.title: Collect and retain only what is necessary by default
controls.section: Principle 2 - Privacy as the Default Setting
controls.requirement: Ensure default settings require no action by the individual to protect their privacy: minimal data collection, shortest necessary retention, and narrowest default sharing.
controls.security_note: Default minimisation directly reduces the volume of data exposed to confidentiality risk.

controls.evidence: Purpose-limitation controls in data architecture (tagging, access scoping)

controls.title: Opt-in, not opt-out, for anything beyond the necessary minimum

controls.requirement: Evaluate and apply techniques such as pseudonymisation, anonymisation, differential privacy, encryption, or federated/on-device learning where they can reduce privacy risk without breaking functionality.

controls.title: Avoid false trade-offs between privacy and functionality/security

controls.requirement: Seek design solutions that achieve both the business/functional goal and strong privacy protection, rather than accepting privacy as the item traded away under time or cost pressure.

controls.title: Protect personal data from collection to secure destruction
controls.section: Principle 5 - End-to-End Security - Full Lifecycle Protection
controls.requirement: Apply appropriate security controls (access control, encryption, monitoring) across the entire data lifecycle: collection, transmission, storage, use, sharing, archiving, and secure deletion/destruction.

controls.section: Principle 5 - End-to-End Security - Full Lifecycle Protection
controls.requirement: Define and enforce retention periods per data category, and ensure secure, verifiable destruction or anonymisation of personal data once no longer needed.
controls.security_note: Timely, verifiable deletion reduces confidentiality exposure from data retained beyond its need.

controls.title: Extend security requirements to third parties in the data chain

controls.requirement: Ensure any processor, sub-processor or partner handling the personal data as part of the design maintains equivalent end-to-end security.
